name: Wi-Fi access point
description: A 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g access point, as a home router is seen from a station across the room: it beacons its SSID every beacon interval, answers probe requests, and authenticates (open system) and associates stations. It reaches the circuit only through the air; its signal reaches a board at the free-space path loss over their distance on the bench.

password.doc: The WPA2-Personal passphrase (8 to 63 characters); empty for an open network

channel.doc: The 2.4 GHz channel (1 to 13, 14 in Japan)

beacon_interval.doc: The time between beacons, in 1024 us time units

bssid.doc: Its MAC address (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff); empty for a locally administered one from its name

outputs.name: mac
outputs.doc: Its MAC address, the network's BSSID

outputs.name: log
outputs.doc: What its stations did: authenticated, associated (with the AID), disassociated, deauthenticated

functional.claims: Beacons (TSF timestamp, interval, ESS and privacy capabilities, SSID, rates, DS parameter set, TIM, ERP, the WPA2-Personal RSN element with a password) every beacon interval at 1 Mbit/s; probe responses to wildcard and matching probe requests; open system authentication; association and reassociation with AIDs from 1; deauthentication and disassociation (IEEE 802.11-2020 9.3.3, 11.3). Frames carry their airtime and reach stations at the free-space path loss over the bench distance (engine/air.h).
omissions: the data path: WPA2's 4-way handshake, DHCP, ARP, ICMP, DNS, TCP and UDP
power save buffering (the TIM is always empty)
the interframe timing of a real AP's firmware: responses follow a received frame after its ACK and DIFS

electrical.claims: As functional: it has no pins.

sources.title: IEEE Std 802.11-2020: frame formats (9.3.3), elements (9.4.2), authentication and association (11.3)
sources.notes: The beacon, probe response, authentication and association frames and their fields; the RSN element of WPA2-Personal (CCMP pairwise and group, PSK).
